staged_prefill.what: prompt in 2048-token batches: each CPU layer's experts stream to the GPU once per 2048 tokens, not per 512

exclusive_tiers.what: experts pinned in VRAM have their RAM pages given back (EDX_PAGEOUT), so RAM only holds experts that are not on a GPU

cpu_lane_overlap.reason: engine-level: llama.cpp's scheduler runs a layer's GPU part and CPU part one after another and syncs with the host between splits; running the CPU's experts while the GPU works needs a split that runs both at once (an engine change, weeks). Costed in leverage.json.

read_pool.edx_pf: EDX_PF mode=2 ops=42103 picked_pages=112839200 resident_at_use=0.9908 prefetch_jobs=290520
read_pool.what: 8 reader threads fetch the picked experts' other matrices (up/down) while the first one computes
read_pool.ab_note: in-process A/B, all arms with MTP drafting on (the per-request switch was ignored in that run)

layer_ahead_prefetch.what: read pool + next layer's experts guessed from the previous token's picks (his trick guesses with the next router; ours below)
layer_ahead_prefetch.his_router_variant: not built: needs the router input at run time inside the CPU path; offline recall of our guessers in predictor_offline.json
layer_ahead_prefetch.ab_note: in-process A/B, all arms with MTP drafting on (the per-request switch was ignored in that run)

no_host_sync.reason: engine-level: llama.cpp's scheduler runs a layer's GPU part and CPU part one after another and syncs with the host between splits; removing the per-layer sync means GPU kernels that poll for experts landing (mapped flags), i.e. replacing ggml's scheduler for MoE layers.

mtp.what: Qwen's own 1-layer draft head guesses 2 tokens ahead, the full model checks them in one pass (exact)

engram_ssd.what: the 28.8 GB n-gram table loaded into RAM (-lzm off) vs read row by row from the SSD (stock default, the baseline)
engram_ssd.note: stock llama.cpp already keeps tables > 4 GiB on disk and reads the ~16 rows a token needs
